shared_elements: coarse granular stone surface with shallow low-relief carving
frontal anthropomorphic composition with a broad upper 'headdress' or crown zone
horizontal band/register of repeated motifs across the upper part
vertical panel or pendant element hanging below a horizontal band
paired symmetrical motifs flanking a central axis
justification: Both show a frontal, axially symmetrical figure organised into a broad banded upper zone of repeated motifs (reading as a headdress or crown) above a wide horizontal band from which a vertical panel descends, all executed in shallow, softly worn relief on a coarse pitted stone with curvilinear volutes and disc forms. The biggest difference is dimensionality and framing: A is a rounded, free-standing boulder sculpture with modelled shoulders and a projecting head photographed in situ, while B is a flat, broken slab whose design is confined to a single carved plane, and their individual motifs (the large chest disc versus B's paired downturned scroll heads) do not match in detail.
